title: How a 1% Fee Quietly Steals Half Your Retirement
description:
A 1% expense ratio sounds tiny. Paid every year, on a balance that keeps compounding, it isn't. We run $100,000 forward 35 years at 7% with no fee, a 1% fee, and a 2% fee, and show exactly how much of your own money the fee actually costs you.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#investingfees #indexfunds #personalfinance

segments.text: A one percent fee sounds tiny. Over thirty-five years, it can cost you literally half of everything you would have had.
Investment fees don't get paid once. They get paid every single year, on a balance that keeps growing. That's the trap.
Start with one hundred thousand dollars, growing at seven percent a year for thirty-five years, completely untouched by fees.
At the full seven percent, that money grows to just over one million dollars.
Now take a fund charging a two percent expense ratio. Same starting amount, same market - but your real return drops to five percent.
That same money grows to about five hundred fifty-two thousand dollars. Roughly half of what it could have been.
Line the outcomes up side by side, and the fee isn't a rounding error. It's the biggest expense of your entire investing life.
The market doesn't decide how much you keep. The fee does.
